title: Rebellion Against the King
summary: Amalekites and Amulonites stirred unconverted Amalekites, Amulonites, and Lamanites to anger against their brethren. Their hatred grew; they rebelled against their king and took up arms against the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi.

explicit_facts.text: The groups described as unconverted were in the lands of Amulon, Helam, and Jerusalem, and in the land round about.
Amalekites and Amulonites stirred them to anger against their brethren.
Their hatred became exceedingly sore, and they began to rebel against their king because they did not want him to be their king.
They took up arms against the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the people and their arms.
The exact place where the rebellion and taking up of arms occurred.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The king is mentioned but is not described as physically present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle; the verses describe taking up arms, not combat.
Do not invent speeches or identify a specific place where the rebellion occurred.

title: The Kingdom Given to His Son
summary: The king confers the kingdom upon his son and calls his name Anti-Nephi-Lehi.

explicit_facts.text: The king conferred the kingdom upon his son and called his name Anti-Nephi-Lehi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king and his son can be shown together during the transfer of the kingdom.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, and manner of the transfer are not stated.

narration.text: Now the king conferred the kingdom upon his son, and he called his name Anti-Nephi-Lehi.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The king's death and the Lamanites' preparations for war are stated in Alma 24:4 but are not depicted as part of this transfer scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the king's death or the Lamanites' preparations as simultaneous with the transfer.
Do not invent a ceremony, spoken words, or a cause of death.

title: From Midian to Ishmael
summary: Ammon, his brethren, and those who had come up with him saw the Lamanites' preparations to destroy their brethren. They came to the land of Midian, where Ammon met all his brethren. From there they came to the land of Ishmael.
characters: those who had come up with Ammon

explicit_facts.text: Ammon, his brethren, and those who had come up with him saw the Lamanites' preparations to destroy their brethren.
They came to the land of Midian, where Ammon met all his brethren.
From Midian they came to the land of Ishmael, intending to hold a council with Lamoni and his brother Anti-Nephi-Lehi about defending themselves against the Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The move from Midian to Ishmael can be shown as travel between the named lands.
unspecified_visual_details: The route and appearance of either land.
Whether the council took place and what anyone said or decided.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse states the purpose of going to Ishmael but does not recount the council itself.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify unnamed brethren or companions by name.
Do not depict council dialogue, a decision, or a completed council.
Do not label Anti-Nephi-Lehi as the people of Ammon.

title: They Will Not Take Up Arms
summary: None of the converted people would take up arms against their brethren or prepare for war; their king also commanded them not to.

explicit_facts.text: Not one of the converted people would take up arms against their brethren.
They would not make preparations for war.
Their king commanded them not to.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king may be shown addressing some of the converted people.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, clothing, and appearances of the people and king.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show an armed confrontation, war preparations, or attribute specific words to the king.
Do not assign the people an identity not stated in this verse.

title: Words to the People
summary: A man addresses the people, thanking God and speaking of the Nephites' preaching, their correspondence, and the recognition of past sins and murders.

explicit_facts.text: He speaks to the people and thanks God for sending the Nephites to preach and convince them of the traditions of their fathers.
He thanks God for a portion of his Spirit to soften their hearts and says they opened correspondence with the Nephites.
He says that through this correspondence they were convinced of their sins and the many murders they had committed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker can be shown addressing listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's identity and appearance.
The gathering's location, size, and arrangement.

spoken_dialogue.text: And behold, I thank my great God that he has given us a portion of his Spirit to soften our hearts,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified male speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: And behold, I also thank my God, that by opening this correspondence we have been convinced of our sins, and of the many murders which we have committed.

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the speaker as a king or name him.

Do not place named Nephite missionaries at the gathering or stage the past murders.

title: Repentance and Forgiveness
summary: A speaker thanks God for granting repentance and forgiving sins and murders. The speaker addresses his brethren and says they did all they could to repent sufficiently before God.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker thanks God for granting them the ability to repent.
The speaker says God forgave their sins and murders and took guilt from their hearts through the merits of his Son.
The speaker addresses his brethren and says they did all they could to repent sufficiently before God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker may be shown addressing a group.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, and appearances of the speaker and those addressed are not described.

title: Keep the Swords Bright
summary: An unidentified speaker addresses brethren, says their swords have become bright, and urges them not to stain their swords with their brethren’s blood but to retain them unstained.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says God has taken away their stains and their swords have become bright.
The speaker urges the brethren not to stain their swords with their brethren’s blood.
The speaker urges them to retain their swords unstained.
The speaker expresses concern that, if they stain their swords again, they may no longer be washed bright through the blood of the Son of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker may be shown addressing a group.
Swords may be shown, but no one is said to handle one during this speech.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and the appearances of the speaker and audience.
Whether swords are physically present during the speech.

spoken_dialogue.text: Now, my best beloved brethren, since God hath taken away our stains, and our swords have become bright, then let us stain our swords no more with the blood of our brethren.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses do not identify the speaker.
The references to stains, washing, and atonement are teachings, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the speaker as the king.
Do not depict blood, combat, or a visible miraculous cleansing of swords.

title: The Plan Made Known
summary: God has shown mercy and made these things known beforehand so the people might not perish. The verse says he loves them and their children and visits them by angels so the plan of salvation may be known to them and future generations.

explicit_facts.text: God has had mercy on the people and made these things known so they might not perish.
God made these things known beforehand because he loves the people and their children.
The verse says God visits them by his angels so the plan of salvation may be known to them and future generations.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse does not narrate a specific angel appearing at this moment or identify a speaker.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an angel appearing in this moment or assign the verse to an identified speaker.

title: Hide the Swords Away
summary: An unidentified speaker praises God's mercy and calls for hiding bright swords as a testimony. The speaker says they will bury the swords if their brethren seek to destroy them, and will go to God and be saved if destroyed.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says their swords are bright and calls for hiding them as a testimony that they have not stained them in the blood of their brethren since God imparted his word to them.
The speaker says they will bury their swords deep in the earth if their brethren seek to destroy them.
The speaker says that if their brethren destroy them, they will go to God and be saved.

unspecified_visual_details: The location, clothing, number of listeners, and appearance of the swords beyond their brightness.

title: The Weapons Buried
summary: After the king finishes speaking, the assembled people bury their swords and other weapons used to shed blood, covenanting not to use them to shed their brethren's blood.

explicit_facts.text: When the king finished speaking and the people were assembled, they buried their swords and all weapons used for shedding blood deep in the earth.
They did this as a testimony to God and men, covenanted not to use weapons to shed blood, and committed to give their own lives rather than shed their brethren's blood.
They covenanted to give to a brother rather than take from him and to labor abundantly rather than spend their days in idleness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The burial can be shown as the people placing weapons into the earth.
unspecified_visual_details: The number of people and weapons, and the burial site's precise appearance.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The covenant is stated in narration; no spoken wording is supplied.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a spoken group vow.

title: Weapons of War for Peace
summary: The Lamanites were brought to believe and know the truth, were firm and willing to suffer death rather than sin, and buried their weapons of war for peace.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites were brought to believe and know the truth.
They were firm and would suffer even unto death rather than commit sin.
They buried their weapons of war for peace.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A retrospective view of the burial place could accompany the narrator's summary without showing a new burial.
unspecified_visual_details: The burial site's appearance and location.
The Lamanites' clothing and individual appearances.

narration.text: And thus we see that, when these Lamanites were brought to believe and to know the truth, they were firm, and would suffer even unto death rather than commit sin; and thus we see that they buried their weapons of peace, or they buried the weapons of war, for peace.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This verse is a narrator's retrospective summary, not a new present-tense event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage a separate burial or an instance of suffering or death.

title: A Warning About Falling Away
summary: The verse teaches that people who have been enlightened and gained knowledge of righteousness become more hardened if they later fall into sin and transgression.

explicit_facts.text: People once enlightened by the Spirit of God and knowledgeable about righteousness become more hardened if they fall into sin and transgression; their state becomes worse than if they had never known these things.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching could be presented as narration over a nonliteral background.
unspecified_visual_details: No specific people, event, location, or visible appearance of the Spirit is described.

narration.text: And thus we can plainly discern, that after a people have been once enlightened by the Spirit of God, and have had great knowledge of things pertaining to righteousness, and then have fallen away into sin and transgression, they become more hardened, and thus their state becomes worse than though they had never known these things.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a teaching, not a narrated visible transformation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Spirit as a visible figure or invent a specific fallen people.
